title.rendered: The Same Power That Raised Christ: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: His incomparably great power for us who believe is that same power He exerted when He raised Christ from the dead. That same power. In you. Right now. This is the engine of every authority the believer walks in.

content.rendered:
His incomparably great power for us who believe is that same power He exerted when He raised Christ from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly realms. That same power. In you. Right now. This is the engine of every authority the believer walks in.

The Gospel For Today | Saturday, July 18, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“I pray also that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened in order that you may know the hope to which he has called you, the riches of his glorious inheritance in his holy people, and his incomparably great power for us who believe. That power is the same as the mighty strength he exerted when he raised Christ from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly realms.”
Ephesians 1:18-20 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Paul is praying for the Ephesian believers to understand something they already possess. Not something they need to acquire. Something already in their spiritual bank account that they have not yet learned to draw on. He prays that the eyes of their heart would be enlightened to see three things. The hope they are called to. The riches of their inheritance in Christ. And, third, His incomparably great power for those who believe.

The Greek word Paul uses for “power” is dunamis. It is the word from which we get the English words “dynamite” and “dynamic.” It means explosive, effective, working power. Then Paul immediately anchors what he means by dunamis with a specific historical comparison. This power is the same as the mighty strength God exerted when He raised Christ from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly realms. The resurrection power. The ascension power. The power that broke the grip of the grave and seated the Son at the right hand of Almighty God.

Read that carefully. The measure of the power available to the believer is not their current sense of strength. Not their spiritual mood on a given morning. Not the last sermon they heard. The measure is the raising of Christ from the dead. If God had to break the grip of hell itself to bring His Son out of the tomb, that same intensity of power is what is at work in you today. Not less. Not a diluted version. The full measure of resurrection power.

This is Paul’s cure for spiritual smallness. Most believers walk through daily life with a sense of their own resources. Their own courage. Their own strength. Their own capacity. Paul says stop. Enlarge the picture. Open the eyes of your heart. The power at work in you today is the same power that raised Jesus from the dead. If it was enough to defeat death, it is more than enough to defeat whatever situation is in front of you this morning.

For Gospelbuzz readers, the truth this morning is expansive. You are not walking into today with your own strength. You are walking into today with resurrection strength inside you by the indwelling Spirit. The situation in front of you is not bigger than the tomb. The tomb could not hold Jesus. Whatever you face today cannot hold what the tomb could not hold. Walk in that reality today.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that Your incomparably great power is at work in me who believes. The same mighty strength You exerted when You raised Christ from the dead and seated Him at Your right hand is the same power operating in my life today. I am not walking into this day with my own resources. I am walking into it with resurrection power inside me by Your Spirit. Whatever situation is in front of me is not bigger than the tomb. The tomb could not hold Jesus. Nothing today can hold what the tomb could not hold. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The same power that raised Christ from the dead is at work in me today. Nothing today is bigger than the tomb the Spirit already broke open. I walk in resurrection power.
